name: gitVisualise
description: Turn any Git repository into an interactive, narrated architecture tour with visual branch history and AI-driven code insights.

paragraphs: gitVisualise is a free tool that turns any GitHub repository into an interactive, narrated architecture tour. Instead of staring at confusing code files, you get a visual map that shows how different parts of a project connect. It's like having a guided tour guide for code.

Whether you're a student trying to understand an open-source project, a manager reviewing your team's work, or a developer onboarding to a new codebase, gitVisualise makes understanding software architecture simple and even fun.
features: Paste & Go – Just copy any GitHub link, paste it into gitVisualise, and instantly see a visual breakdown of the entire project.
Narrated Tours – Each visualization comes with plain-English explanations of what each component does and how they work together.
Zero Installation Hassle – Runs entirely in your browser. No downloads, no setup, no technical knowledge required.
Multiple Ways to Use – Access it as a website, a command-line tool, a Claude Code skill, or a GitHub Action.
100% Free & Open Source – Contribute improvements, report issues, or suggest new features. Everyone is welcome.

requirements.text: No technical jargon – just clear explanations like "This file handles user login" or "This section manages the database connection."
